newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hashimoto still sceptical of Lima hostage release.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto still sceptical of Lima hostage release.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto reaffirmed on Saturday his scepticism about the possible release of hostages from the Japanese Ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I don't view the situation optimistically," he told a news conference, adding: "I will continue to support the Peruvian government."

Hashimoto's comment echoes his statement two days ago following the recent release of seven hostages that the seige would become more tense as the number of captives -- now 74 people, including top Peruvian government officials -- nears a level the rebels can control.

There have been no negotiations between the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement rebels and the Peru government since last week's face-to-face talks between the government's negotiator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo and the rebels.

The Japanese premier repeated that he would not be cancelling his planned tour of Southeast Asia. Hashimoto is scheduled to leave next Tuesday for an eight-day trip to Brunei, Malaysia, India, Vietnam and Singapore.
